sections.assessment: Accurately states the relevant correction: operator names are prescribed, with plus and minus as examples.
Identifies the misconception but says only ‘it seems’ without explaining why arbitrary names might be assumed.
The consequence is unclear: an arbitrary function name would simply not be selected for a + expression; ‘не находил бы нужный метод’ leaves unclear which lookup fails.
Conveys a mapping from symbols to names, but ‘каждому символу’ overstates the rule because only supported operators have conventions.
Correctly contrasts the translation of a + b to plus with the distractor's minus claim.
‘Операторы путают’ names confusion but does not specify the likely plus/minus mix-up.
Gives a direct logical consequence of the false translation: addition would invoke subtraction.
The compact mapping + to plus directly corrects the specific error.
Correctly states that the mechanism uses a function marked operator rather than a separate special operator construct.
The explanation is too generic to identify what feature of the mechanism could be mistaken.
‘Перегрузка была бы иной’ gives no concrete or testable consequence of the proposed special construct.
Names the required operator fun form and fixed-name convention, though it omits that implementations may be extensions.
States the core convention, but ‘за каждым оператором’ should be read as each supported operator; Kotlin has a predefined supported set.
Shows both the plus declaration name and the a.plus(b) translation correctly.
Offers a useful design heuristic; vectors are a natural example, while money depends on domain semantics.
These are examples from several convention groups, not an edge case; list is illustrative and not exhaustive.
‘operator обязателен’ is too absolute: it is required on the declaration, but an override of an operator function may omit the modifier.

corrected_ANSC.assessment: All four options respond to what operator overloading is: A and C state false declaration rules, B gives a specific translation claim, and D states the convention. B is somewhat narrower because it describes only the plus-to-method mapping rather than defining the broader mechanism, but it still addresses the question; this is a completeness distinction, not a factual-accuracy judgment.

corrected_SFPL.assessment: Assessing form and tone alone: A uses emphatic ‘любой’ and ‘произвольным’; B alone gives a concrete expression and method call; C has an awkward function-versus-operator contrast; D is a fluent general definition. There is no basis to fail SFPL merely because D is true or because other claims are false. A, C, and D mention operator/operator modifier, and B also states a concrete operator translation.

concrete_limits: This follow-up assesses the 17 exact section fields and the wording of the four options only.
It does not re-evaluate the primary-source facts or alter the saved raw Q29 review.
The D.related caveat applies to overrides: a declaration introduces operator, while an override can inherit the operator contract without repeating the modifier.
